title: Which side of the road do vehicles drive on in Latvia?
shortAnswer: Vehicles drive on the right-hand side of the road.
answer: Traffic in Latvia keeps to the right. Overtaking is normally performed on the left unless road signs or markings indicate otherwise.
tips: Be extra careful during your first few days of driving.
Watch for tram tracks in Riga.

title: Can I use my Indian driving licence in Latvia?
shortAnswer: It depends on your residence status and Latvian regulations.
answer: Students staying in Latvia for a longer period should verify whether their licence remains valid or must be exchanged according to Latvian law.

title: Do I need an International Driving Permit?
shortAnswer: It depends on your licence and residency status.
answer: Some foreign drivers carry an International Driving Permit together with their original licence. Always verify current CSDD requirements.
tips: Carry the original licence as well.

title: Are seat belts mandatory?
shortAnswer: Yes.
answer: Drivers and passengers must use seat belts where fitted. Child passengers should use an appropriate child restraint when required.
tips: Ensure every passenger is buckled before moving.

title: Is drink driving allowed?
shortAnswer: Latvia has strict drink-driving laws.
answer: Never drive after consuming alcohol. Penalties can be severe depending on the circumstances.
tips: Use public transport or a taxi if you've been drinking.

title: Can I use my phone while driving?
shortAnswer: Avoid using a handheld phone while driving.
answer: Drivers should avoid distractions and comply with Latvian regulations regarding mobile phone use while operating a vehicle.

title: Are winter tyres required?
shortAnswer: Winter tyres are required during the official winter season.
answer: Vehicles must comply with Latvian seasonal tyre requirements. Check current CSDD dates each year.

title: Do headlights need to be switched on?
shortAnswer: Drivers must comply with Latvian lighting requirements.
answer: Vehicle lighting requirements vary depending on conditions and regulations. Check CSDD guidance.
tips: Check all exterior lights before driving.

title: What should I do after a traffic accident?
shortAnswer: Ensure safety first and follow Latvian procedures.
answer: Move to a safe location if possible, assist injured persons, contact emergency services if required, and exchange information with other parties.

title: Where can I find official driving rules in Latvia?
shortAnswer: The official source is CSDD.
answer: The Road Traffic Safety Directorate (CSDD) publishes official guidance, driver services, examinations and road safety information.
tips: Always verify legal information from official sources.

title: What are the general speed limits in Latvia?
shortAnswer: Speed limits depend on the type of road and are indicated by traffic signs.
answer: Always follow posted speed limit signs. Different limits apply within cities, outside built-up areas and on highways. Temporary limits may also apply due to weather or road works.
tips: Watch for temporary road work signs.

title: Do trams have priority in Latvia?
shortAnswer: In many situations, yes.
answer: Trams often have priority according to Latvian traffic regulations. Always pay attention to traffic signs, road markings and traffic lights.
tips: Be especially careful when driving in Riga.

title: Can I park anywhere on the street?
shortAnswer: No. Parking restrictions are indicated by road signs.
answer: Many city areas have paid parking or restricted parking zones. Always read nearby parking signs before leaving your vehicle.

title: Can police stop vehicles for inspection?
shortAnswer: Yes.
answer: Police may stop vehicles to verify documents, conduct traffic enforcement or perform safety inspections.

title: Which documents should I carry while driving?
shortAnswer: Carry all legally required identification and vehicle documents.
answer: Drivers should carry the documents required under Latvian law, including personal identification and vehicle documentation where applicable.

title: Are dash cameras legal in Latvia?
shortAnswer: They are commonly used, but recordings must respect privacy and applicable laws.
answer: Dash cameras may be used responsibly. If recordings contain personal data, privacy rules may apply.
tips: Avoid publishing recordings containing personal information without considering legal requirements.

title: Can I overtake on any road?
shortAnswer: No.
answer: Overtaking is prohibited in certain locations and situations. Always obey road signs, markings and visibility requirements.
tips: Never overtake at pedestrian crossings or where prohibited.

title: What should I do if my vehicle breaks down?
shortAnswer: Move to a safe place and seek assistance.
answer: Turn on hazard warning lights, move the vehicle if safe, and contact roadside assistance if necessary.
tips: Wear a reflective vest if exiting on a roadway.

title: What emergency number should drivers call?
shortAnswer: Call 112 for emergencies.
answer: The European emergency number 112 connects callers to emergency services in Latvia.

title: Where can I learn Latvian traffic rules?
shortAnswer: The official source is CSDD.
answer: The Road Traffic Safety Directorate (CSDD) provides official information for drivers, examinations, licensing and road safety.
tips: Always rely on official guidance before making legal decisions.

title: What should I do when approaching a pedestrian crossing?
shortAnswer: Slow down and give way to pedestrians when required.
answer: Drivers should approach pedestrian crossings carefully, remain alert for people crossing, and comply with Latvian traffic regulations regarding pedestrian priority.
tips: Reduce speed near schools and residential areas.

title: Can I drive during heavy snowfall?
shortAnswer: Yes, but only if your vehicle is prepared for winter conditions.
answer: Winter weather can reduce visibility and road grip. Drive at a safe speed, increase following distance and ensure your vehicle is equipped according to seasonal requirements.
tips: Clear snow from all windows before driving.

title: Should I keep a safe following distance?
shortAnswer: Yes. Always maintain enough distance to stop safely.
answer: Following too closely increases the risk of collisions, especially during rain, snow or icy conditions.

title: Can I park on a pedestrian crossing?
shortAnswer: No.
answer: Parking on or near pedestrian crossings is prohibited where restricted by Latvian traffic regulations.
tips: Always check road signs before parking.

title: What should I do if an emergency vehicle approaches?
shortAnswer: Give way safely.
answer: Drivers should allow emergency vehicles with active warning signals to pass as quickly and safely as possible.

title: Is vehicle insurance mandatory?
shortAnswer: Yes. Vehicles must have the required insurance before being driven.
answer: Motor vehicles must comply with Latvian insurance requirements before using public roads.

title: Can cyclists use the road?
shortAnswer: Yes. Drivers should safely share the road with cyclists.
answer: Cyclists have rights and responsibilities under Latvian traffic regulations. Maintain a safe distance when overtaking.

title: What should I do if I hit a wild animal?
shortAnswer: Stop safely and contact the appropriate authorities if required.
answer: Wildlife collisions can occur outside urban areas. Secure the scene, avoid unnecessary risks and notify emergency services or police when appropriate.

title: Should I use hazard warning lights?
shortAnswer: Use them only when appropriate.
answer: Hazard warning lights help warn other road users when your vehicle creates an unexpected hazard or is stopped due to an emergency.
tips: Turn them off once the hazard has ended.

title: Where can I check the latest Latvian driving regulations?
shortAnswer: Use official government websites.
answer: Always verify legal or procedural information through the official Latvian Road Traffic Safety Directorate (CSDD) or other relevant government authorities before making decisions.
tips: Avoid relying only on social media or forums for legal advice.

title: Can I turn right on a red traffic light?
shortAnswer: No, unless a specific traffic sign allows it.
answer: Drivers must obey traffic lights. A right turn on red is only permitted where explicitly indicated by official road signs.

title: Should children use child safety seats?
shortAnswer: Yes, where required by Latvian law.
answer: Children must be transported using appropriate child restraint systems according to applicable Latvian regulations.
tips: Never hold a child on your lap while driving.

title: Do pedestrians always have priority?
shortAnswer: Drivers must comply with pedestrian priority rules at crossings.
answer: Approach crossings carefully and be prepared to stop whenever required by Latvian traffic regulations.

title: Can I drive with headphones?
shortAnswer: Avoid anything that reduces awareness while driving.
answer: Drivers should remain fully aware of surrounding traffic and emergency vehicles at all times.
tips: Keep your hearing unobstructed while driving.

title: Can I stop on a motorway shoulder?
shortAnswer: Only in emergencies.
answer: The emergency shoulder should only be used when absolutely necessary, such as vehicle breakdowns or emergencies.

title: Should I carry a reflective safety vest?
shortAnswer: Yes. It is recommended and may be legally required in certain situations.
answer: If you need to leave your vehicle after a breakdown or accident, wearing a reflective vest improves visibility and safety.
tips: Keep the vest inside the passenger compartment.

title: Should I keep emergency equipment in my car?
shortAnswer: Yes.
answer: Keeping basic emergency equipment such as a warning triangle, first-aid kit and reflective vest helps you deal safely with unexpected situations.
tips: Check expiry dates of first-aid supplies.

title: Are roads slippery during autumn?
shortAnswer: Yes. Wet leaves and rain can significantly reduce tyre grip.
answer: Drivers should reduce speed during autumn and early winter when road conditions may deteriorate rapidly.

title: Can I use cruise control during snow or ice?
shortAnswer: It is generally safer to avoid cruise control on slippery roads.
answer: Drivers should maintain full control of acceleration and braking during adverse weather conditions.
tips: Drive smoothly and avoid sudden steering movements.

title: Where can I report dangerous road conditions?
shortAnswer: Contact the responsible road authority or emergency services if immediate danger exists.
answer: Hazards such as fallen trees, damaged road surfaces or objects blocking the road should be reported to the appropriate authority.
tips: If lives are at risk, call 112 immediately.

title: Should I check weather conditions before driving?
shortAnswer: Yes, especially during winter.
answer: Latvia experiences snow, ice, fog and heavy rain during different seasons. Checking the weather before a journey helps you prepare and drive safely.
tips: Allow extra travel time during winter.

officialSources.name: Latvian Environment, Geology and Meteorology Centre

title: Can foreign tourists rent a car in Latvia?
shortAnswer: Yes, if they meet the rental company's requirements.
answer: Rental companies may have minimum age, licence duration and documentation requirements. Check directly with the rental provider.

title: Is speeding monitored by cameras?
shortAnswer: Yes. Speed enforcement cameras operate in Latvia.
answer: Drivers should always obey posted speed limits as violations may be detected using automated enforcement systems.
tips: Drive according to posted limits rather than relying on navigation apps.

title: Should I remove snow from my vehicle before driving?
shortAnswer: Yes.
answer: Snow or ice on the roof, windows and lights can create hazards for you and other road users.
tips: Clear all windows, mirrors and lights.

title: Can I use summer tyres all year?
shortAnswer: No. Latvia has seasonal tyre requirements.
answer: Vehicles must comply with official tyre regulations during winter periods.
tips: Check tyre tread before every winter season.

title: What should I do if I see black ice?
shortAnswer: Reduce speed immediately and avoid sudden movements.
answer: Black ice can be difficult to see and greatly reduces traction. Drive smoothly and increase following distance.

title: Should I keep enough fuel during winter trips?
shortAnswer: Yes.
answer: Cold weather and unexpected delays can increase fuel consumption. Keeping sufficient fuel improves safety during long journeys.

title: Should I use winter windshield washer fluid?
shortAnswer: Yes.
answer: Winter washer fluid helps maintain visibility by preventing freezing in cold temperatures.

title: Can I drive through flooded roads?
shortAnswer: Avoid flooded roads whenever possible.
answer: Floodwater may hide hazards or damage the vehicle. Choose an alternative route if conditions appear unsafe.

title: Where can I find official information about driving in Latvia?
shortAnswer: Use CSDD as the primary official source.
answer: The Road Traffic Safety Directorate (CSDD) provides official information about driving licences, vehicle registration, road safety, traffic regulations and driver services in Latvia.
tips: Always verify legal information using official government websites.
